description.p: NOMM is a stupid simple, super clean "native" (as in it runs on Linux without having to use translation tools...) mod manager for Linux. The goal here is to keep the setup really simple for users like me who don't need the super advanced/complex features. Just a few clicks on a clean, modern interface, and you're done :)
Don't expect NOMM to manage mods for something like Skyrim. There are specific tools for that (see NaK or Jackify).
Instead, think of NOMM as more of a general purpose tool for most games that just need you to point to a directory and extract some mod archives.

ul.li: Feature: Overhaul UX of mods and downloads tabs when no mods installed
Feature: Overhaul mod upgrade / downgrade flow on downloads tab when downloading an update for a mod
Feature: Can now install different versions or variants of mods side-by-side
Feature: Add buttons to open utility staging and download folders on utility tab
Change: Hide action bars on mods and downloads tabs when no mods installed

Change: No longer get NOMM latest version from Github releases when opening settings menu. NOMM latest version is now obatined from Flathub at app start. This should make opening the settings menu more snappier and limit calls to Github API.
Fix: NOMM version button can no longer be clicked on dev versions (if you want access to dev versions to help with testing, they are on Discord)
Fix: Github asset matching now properly uses regex as expected instead of simple substring match
Feature: Can now install non-archive utilities
Feature: Can now ignore mod updates so that they stop showing in the UI
Fix: Fix additional cases of NOMM not detecting a downloaded utility
Fix: Regression from 0.14.2 causing an error during onboarding after the Nexus API key input
Feature: Add support for unofficial Eden Flatpak
Flatpak: Upgrade Gnome environment to version 51 (latest)
Fix: Correctly remove selected utility when multiple utilities are listed and clicking on trash button
Fix: Better downloaded utility archive recognition
Fix: Unauthenticated Github API calls will be made more sparingly
Change: Add Steam installation validation to avoid NOMM selecting a broken Steam installation instead of a functioning one
Fix: Issue with permissions for custom staging/download paths
Major overhaul of utility management
New: Nexus, Github and Flathub can be added as sources to download utilities
New: Set utilities as being incompatible with other utilities
New: Launch Linux utilities
New: Launch Windows utilities (with Wine, downloaded at runtime)
New: Wine and Wine prefix management from within NOMM
New: Support for Wine verbs and installation via Winetricks
New: Launch Flatpak utilities
Change: Much more intuitive utility blacklist/whitelist support
Change: Overhaul utility tab UI with new icons, buttons, interactions
Change: Completely overhauled the configuration builder to reflect these changes
Change: Adding launch options is now super easy and won't require relaunching Steam
Change: Better detection of removed Steam libraries (better permissions request flow)
Fix two regressions impacting Nexus one-click downloads
Fix refresh metadata not working when no mods were downloaded previously
